name: Romania

paths.name: Holding the portfolio personally (ordinary residence)
paths.note: Dividends and gains on shares sold through a foreign broker both bear 16% from 2026; the foreign withholding is credited up to the Romanian tax, so a treaty-rate 15% leaves 1% on foreign dividends. A Romanian broker would withhold 3% on gains from holdings over a year, but the model scores the foreign-broker case. A health contribution (CASS) of at most RON 9,720 a year is not counted. No wealth tax on securities; children inherit free of inheritance tax if the succession is finalised within 2 years.

checks.working: Top marginal rates; the family is tax resident, taxed on income from any source (Fiscal Code art. 59, art. 130). Dividends of 1,000,000, all foreign, with 15% withheld at source (150,000). Dividends distributed from 1 January 2026 bear 16% (art. 97(7) as amended by Law 141/2025): 16% x 1,000,000 = 160,000, declared in the single return. The foreign tax is credited where a double tax treaty applies, per country and per source of income, up to the Romanian tax on that income (art. 131; norms point 46): 150,000 is below 160,000, so the credit is 150,000 and the Romanian tax on dividends is 10,000. Gains of 500,000 on shares sold through a foreign broker: no Romanian intermediary withholds (the 3%/6% final tax applies only to Romanian intermediaries and permanent establishments), so the net annual gain is declared in the single return and taxed at 16% from 1 January 2026 (Law 239/2025): 16% x 500,000 = 80,000. Wealth tax: none on securities. Total 10,000 + 80,000 = 90,000. The health contribution CASS (10% of a base capped at 24 minimum gross salaries = RON 97,200, i.e. RON 9,720; art. 155(1) and art. 170) is a social contribution and is left out, as in the tax file. Assumes a treaty with the source country applies and that the family has no losses to net.

Romania levies no inheritance or gift tax on money or securities, and none on real estate when the succession is debated and finalised before a notary (certificate of heir) within 2 years of death (Fiscal Code art. 111 para. (3)); the 1% charge applies only if the term is missed. The family is assumed to finalise within 2 years. Each of the three children inherits 16,666,666.67 and pays no tax: total 0. Notary fees for the succession procedure are not a tax and are left out.

assumptions: The family are EU citizens who move in and become Romanian tax residents (more than 183 days or centre of vital interests in Romania); they register their residence with the immigration office.

Gains on foreign shares are scored at 16%, which assumes a foreign broker. Through a Romanian broker the final withholding is 3% on holdings over 365 days (6% under); whether foreign-listed shares held through a Romanian broker qualify was not confirmed, so the lower rate is not used.
Foreign withholding of 15% is creditable because a double tax treaty exists with the source country (Romania has about 89); where it does not, nothing is credited (art. 131).
The health contribution CASS (10%, base capped at RON 97,200, at most RON 9,720 a year) is not included in the annual checks, as in the tax file.
The family home (EUR 5m) bears the 0.9% special tax on the tax value above RON 2.5m (tax file); the annual checks use securities only and do not test it.
Succession is finalised within 2 years of each death, so the 1% charge does not arise.

No Romanian holding company is projected: dividends and gains in an SRL bear 16% corporate tax (the participation exemption needs a 10% stake held for a year, which a diversified portfolio lacks), and the owner then pays 16% on every payout, so the SRL is never better than holding personally. Romania has no trust, and a Romanian foundation cannot distribute to its founder.
open_questions: The 16% rate on foreign-source dividends and the 16% rate on gains via a foreign broker rest on PwC, Kinstellar and Fiscalitatea.ro; art. 97(7), art. 131 and the Law 239/2025 text were not opened in the consolidated Fiscal Code.
Whether foreign-listed shares sold through a Romanian broker bear the 3% final tax (art. 96^1 Fiscal Code) was not confirmed, and so the cheaper Romanian-broker route is not scored.
The family home's special tax (0.9% above RON 2.5m of tax value) is in the tax file, but the checks cannot test it; whether the threshold is per building or per owner is not settled.
Scope of the 1% charge on late successions (real estate only, or the whole estate) is disputed in the sources; it does not affect the checks.

Health contribution (CASS): 10% of investment income, capped at 24 minimum wages (RON 97,200 for 2026, so at most RON 9,720 a year per person; RON 19,440 if both spouses reach the cap). It is a real annual cost not in the tax file or the projection (about EUR 2,000-4,000 a year); the engine has no capped contribution.
